text:
sam.security: Heads-up: we're going to give CI the ability to sign builds in private/on-prem installs. Need concrete minimal RBAC + netpol + audit guidance so a compromised runner can't sign arbitrary artifacts. Also want a tabletop sim. Tagging @liam-crypto @jenna-sre.

jenna-sre: Short answer: ephemeral principal + signing-only path through an HSM/KMS proxy. CI should NOT hold long-term keys. Netpol: egress-only to proxy CIDRs and block all other external egress. Example in k8s below.

liam-crypto: KMS policy: allow kms:Sign scoped to `arn:redwood:kms:region:acct:key/ci-signer-v1` and resource path conditions for the artifact prefix. Deny kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey for CI role. Require attestation token as a condition (TPM or instance attestation) with nonce. Log every Sign call to an immutable audit sink.

akshay-devex: Audit forwarding note: in private deployments we should push logs into the customers SIEM (push or syslog endpoint) or write to customer-controlled object store. Avoid duplicating logs to Redwood unless customer opts in. We'll create CI verify hooks that consult the revocation list and timestamp.

nora-privacy: Retention defaults: 90d, configurable up to customer policy. MUST filter PII from command args and envs before exporting. Add an opt-in field in install config for sending to Redwood-hosted analytics.

ops-oncall: Runbook: on detection of runner compromise -> revoke CI signing principal, rotate key, add signer cert serial to revocation list, block artifact promotion. Note: previously-signed artifacts still verify unless we embed short-lived signer certs and check revocation/attestation at verify time. Recommend signer cert TTL <= 1h for CI flows.

jenna-sre: Netpol example (restrict egress):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: ci-egress-to-kms-proxy
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ci-runner
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.200.8.5/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Also add a deny-all egress policy for other pods in the same namespace except controller/sidecars that need it.

liam-crypto: KMS policy snippet (conceptual): `Allow: kms:Sign on resource arn:redwood:kms:us-west-2:987654:key/ci-signer-v1; Condition: StringEquals kms:SigningAlgorithm RSA_SSA_PKCS1_2048; StringLike kms:ResourcePrefix artifacts/ci/*; Bool: AttestationPresent true` and bind `aws:SourceIp` to the proxy address.

akshay-devex: For the PR, I'll add a CI job that calls `/verify?artifact=sha256:...` which will validate signature + check revocation list + attestation timestamp before promoting. We should also add an opt-in metric to surface signing failures.

sam.security: Tabletop sim please: steps we want: 1) deploy pod with label `app=ci-runner` but with attacker image; 2) try direct TCP connect to KMS backend IP (should fail); 3) try connect through kms-proxy (should be allowed only with valid attestation); 4) attempt kube-apiserver token swap to move laterally (should be blocked by RBAC and network policy). Jenna, can you run this Friday morning?

jenna-sre: I'll schedule Fri 09:30. Will use `netpol-sim` harness + a fake attestation responder so we can test failures. I'll post a draft PR template in #eng-releases with sample policies and a checklist: minimal SA permissions, ephemeral creds, attestation requirement, audit sink config, retention options, legal loop.

kms-bot: Note: key `ci-signer-v1` rotation scheduled 2024-09-02T02:00Z. Audit export endpoints: pending mapping per-customer.

ops-oncall: One more: instrument detection rules for unusual sign volume or signer IP anomalies; tie to automated revocation playbook.

sam.security: Great. After Jenna posts the PR I'll route to @legal and @platform for sign-off. Thanks everyone.
